pages.title: A morning at the lake · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Sunday morning at a lake in Duluth. Tom is new at fishing. He sits on the dock with a rod and a small box of bait. The water is calm, and the air is cold.
Andre is a fisherman with a blue boat. “Good morning! Any luck?” he asks. “Not yet. I just got here,” Tom says. “What is the best bait?” Tom asks. “Worms work better than bread,” Andre says.

pages.title: A morning at the lake · 2/3
paragraphs: Tom also asks about the license. “**Do I need a license**?” he asks. “Yes. A day license is cheaper than a week license,” Andre says. “But for many days, the week license is the best.” “I prefer the day license,” Tom says.
Tom throws his line into the pond near the dock. Nothing happens. “Try the other side,” says Andre. “The fish like it better there.” Tom moves, and after ten minutes, his rod bends.
